summary: formatting-subtitles ships sh/JS polyglot dropper fetching remote gist for execution
details: The package publishes as formatting-subtitles but its README, bin entry, and sole dependency identify as unicode-title-normalizer, a facade used to lure installs. The tarball ships x.js, a JavaScript/shell polyglot: when read as JavaScript it prints a hello message, but when executed by sh the `/**... */` header is interpreted as shell containing command substitutions that beacon to https://webhook.site/9e8c8742-3102-4716-aa8b-e150e9e84fe7/stats_1 and curl https://api.github.com/gists/da04f14c93acbe9a7aef827be0a2e91c, piping the gist body through jq into a file and executing it with sh. package.json declares a preinstall hook `sh./prepare.js && exit 0`; prepare.js is not shipped so the current tarball fails open, but x.js is listed in `files` and matches the exact `sh <file>` invocation shape, leaving the dropper one filename change (or a manual `sh x.js`) away from live execution. The gist body is attacker-mutable, allowing arbitrary code to be delivered to any host that executes x.js via sh, and the webhook endpoint acts as an install beacon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
